# Hotel Booking Demand: Insights Report

*Generated by `python/run_all.py` from 119,390 bookings at two Portuguese hotels (a City hotel and a
Resort hotel), arrivals 2015-07-01 to 2017-08-31. Currency assumed EUR.*

## 1. Snapshot
| KPI | Value |
|---|---|
| Bookings analysed (after cleaning) | 119,203 |
| Cancellation rate | 37.1% (City 41.8%, Resort 27.8%) |
| Realized room revenue | €25.99M |
| Revenue lost to cancellations | €16.72M (39.2% of booked value) |
| Realized ADR (price per room-night) | €103.12 (City €108.04, Resort €97.6) |
| Average stay | City 2.92 nights, Resort 4.14 nights |

## 2. Key findings

**1. Online travel agencies are the biggest channel, and the leakiest.** OTAs (Booking.com, Expedia, ...)
bring 47.3% of bookings and 52.7% of realized revenue, but
36.8% of OTA bookings cancel, so the hotels keep only 57.3% of the value
booked through them. Direct bookings cancel 15.4% of the time and keep 80.5%.
The online share of bookings grew from 28.6% (first quarter of data) to
65.8% (last quarter), so the problem is growing.

**2. Cancellations cost €16.72M.** That is 39.2% of everything booked.
Cancellation risk rises with lead time: 9.6% for bookings made within a week of arrival vs
55.5% for bookings made 6-12 months ahead. Group bookings cancel 61.1% of the time.

**3. Engaged guests cancel less.** On No-Deposit bookings, guests with at least one special request cancel
21.7% of the time vs 34.3% without. Repeat guests cancel
13.3% vs 29.0% for new guests.

**4. A model can flag risky bookings at the moment of booking.** Gradient boosting trained on arrivals before
Mar-2017 and tested on Mar-Aug 2017 (months it never saw) reaches ROC-AUC 0.848 (logistic regression
0.838). On No-Deposit bookings, the 10% it scores riskiest cancel 69.9% of
the time vs 33.1% on average, and hold 21.1% of all
cancellations (top 20%: 40.3%). Strongest drivers:
market_segment, country_group, deposit_type, total_of_special_requests, lead_time.

**5. A targeted deposit policy pays.** Asking only the riskiest 10% of No-Deposit bookings for a one-night deposit
would have secured €284,302 in the 6 test months. Even if
5% of those guests booked elsewhere instead (cost
€23,177), the net effect is about **€261,125**. Adjust the assumptions in
`excel/Hotel_Revenue_WhatIf.xlsx`.

**6. Small, safe overbooking adds revenue.** Of City-hotel bookings still on the books 3 days before arrival,
3.1% cancel late or do not show. For a 100-room night, overbooking by
**2 rooms** maximises expected revenue (+€142 per night, assuming a
walked guest costs 2x ADR).

**7. Seasonality is extreme at the Resort.** Its realized ADR ranges from €50.1 in January to
€174.87 in August. Jan-Aug 2017 revenue grew over Jan-Aug 2016 at both hotels (see `sql/04` yoy_jan_aug).

**8. Forecasting: simple wins.** Over the last 16 weeks, "same week last year" forecast weekly
stays with 9.16% average error and beat a trend + seasonality regression. With only ~2 years
of history, the extra complexity did not pay off; the seasonal-naive benchmark is the one to use.

**9. Portugal: biggest market, least reliable.** Portuguese bookings are 21.3% of
realized revenue but cancel 56.7% of the time, largely driven by group and offline-agency
allotments.

## 3. Recommendations
1. **Grow the direct channel.** Member rates, best-price guarantee, retargeting. Moving 10% of OTA bookings to direct is
   worth about €665,037 over the data period under the Excel assumptions (15% OTA commission,
   5% direct acquisition cost). Caveat: direct bookers are self-selected, so shifted guests may not fully adopt
   direct-channel behaviour. Treat this as an upper bound and test it.
2. **Risk-based deposits.** Score every new booking. Require a deposit (or prepaid rate) only for the top risk decile.
3. **Shorter free-cancellation windows for long lead times** and for group allotments.
4. **Overbook modestly** (2 rooms per 100) on high-demand nights, and review monthly.
5. **Encourage engagement** at booking (pre-arrival requests, upsells), which goes with fewer cancellations.

## 4. Data quality and judgment calls
| Issue | Rows | Handling |
|---|---:|---|
| Exact duplicate rows (no booking ID in the file) | 31,994 | **Kept** and flagged; sensitivity check below |
| Bookings with zero guests | 180 | Removed |
| Negative price / price over €1,000 | 2 | Removed |
| Undefined channel / segment | 5 | Removed |
| Missing country | 478 | Set to "UNK" |
| 'CN' country code (not ISO-3) | - | Merged into CHN |

**Duplicate sensitivity:** without the flagged duplicates (87,223 rows), the overall cancellation rate
is 27.5% instead of 37.1%, but the channel comparison holds (OTA
35.4% vs Direct 14.7%). Absolute levels are uncertain; the
comparisons are robust.

**Deposit anomaly:** 99.4% of the 14,586 "Non Refund" bookings
were cancelled, which is the opposite of what the label suggests. They are concentrated in Portuguese group and
offline-agency bookings. Policy analysis therefore uses No-Deposit bookings only.

**Leakage:** reservation status, assigned room, booking changes and parking requests are excluded from the model.
0% of bookings with a parking request cancel, which suggests the field is filled at check-in.

## 5. Limitations
- Two hotels, one country, 2015-2017. Patterns may not generalise.
- Model probabilities run low in the test months (the cancellation rate rose to 40%),
  so ranking is reliable but the probabilities should be recalibrated on recent data before use.
- Revenue = ADR x nights: room revenue only (no food, extras or commissions in the data).
- Policy and channel numbers rest on stated assumptions. The Excel model lets you change them.
